question: Can a constant-depth quantum circuit reliably compute parity?
idea: Parity records whether a bit string has an odd number of ones. In the specified circuit model with polynomially many qubits, the manuscript claims constant depth cannot achieve any fixed positive worst-case advantage. The available gates, zero-initialized ancillas and single measured output are explicit restrictions on the claim.
why: Mathematics used to understand physical models, including quantum systems and interacting particles. A theorem concerns a specified model, not every physical situation.

glossary.meaning: A mathematical statement proposed to be true but requiring proof or a counterexample.

exactClaim: Resolves Moore's parity conjecture in the measured-output model: constant-depth quantum circuits with arbitrary one-qubit gates, unbounded-arity Toffoli gates and polynomially many total qubits cannot compute parity with any fixed positive worst-case advantage. Ancillas start in zero, one output qubit is measured, and all other registers may be discarded. Xu–Li's reductions give the same bounded-error obstruction for strict majority. )
